items.title: Attribution Bias in Philosophical Knowledge Graphs: Corpus Frequency versus Temporal Sourcing
items.abstract: arXiv:2606.29070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational knowledge graphs assign philosophical concepts to traditions based on corpus frequency: the school that mentions a concept most becomes its attributed tradition. We argue this conflates three measurements: textual power, historical priority, and philosophical significance, demonstrated using the darshana-graph, a knowledge graph of 28,322 relationships across Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions.
